latest_final: Kameda was a king locked in a court power struggle with Umio, a political rival. Kameda ordered Umio’s assassination, and the struggle ended with Umio’s faction defeated. Kameda’s body was cremated, the ordinary funerary custom for a king, so its fragmentation did not mean he had lost. Umio’s body was buried by Kameda’s faction; burial was not itself a disgrace, but the fact that Umio’s opponents controlled his remains showed that his faction could no longer determine his fate or carry out its own rites. People therefore judged Umio the likely political loser, even though his body was intact and Kameda’s was reduced to fragments.
